mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
regime_hint: Rising inflationary bias in FOMC communications
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from a pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% in any month during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE above 6.5% for two consecutive months coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-force participation reduces supply-side constraints.
failure_condition: In a 200-day window, the 60-day forward return is not statistically superior to a baseline of low-unemployment periods (t-test p > 0.05), or UNRATE never exceeds 6.5% consecutively in the window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly expansion in INDPRO above 105 with a rising HOUST series predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as growing industrial production and housing starts signal economic momentum.
failure_condition: Across 50 windows, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive when both INDPRO > 105 and HOUST is rising (two-tailed test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both GDPC1 and PAYEMS exceeding 2% signals weak consumer and employment demand, leading to a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < prev AND PAYEMS < prev by > 2%
failure_condition: Over 40 windows, the 5-day forward return is not significantly negative when both proxies fall by more than 2% (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in CPIAUCSL below 105 for three consecutive months indicates disinflation, which is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as rate-cut expectations rise.
failure_condition: In 40 windows where CPIAUCSL < 105 for 3 months, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PAYEMS below 120,000 followed by a sustained rise in UNRATE above 7%, predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as weak hiring and tighter labor markets depress equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 120000 AND UNRATE > 7% for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market softening with wage moderation
failure_condition: Across 30 windows, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative when the defined labor-market regime occurs (bootstrap p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly cross of INDPRO > 110 and RSAFS > 350M coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as strong industrial output and retail sales suggest resilient supply chains.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 110 AND RSAFS > 350000000 for the month
failure_condition: In 50 windows, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive when both proxies are above their thresholds (two-tailed test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in HOUST below 650 units for four consecutive months in a regime of rising UNRATE (>7%) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to weak housing demand and tighter credit conditions.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 650 for 4 consecutive months AND UNRATE > 7%
regime_hint: Credit tightening and housing weakness regime
failure_condition: In 40 windows with the specified regime, the 60-day forward return is not significantly negative (bootstrap p > 0.05).
